```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Diet is one of the eight components of the American Heart Association's
(AHA) Life's Essential 8 (LE8).
`essential8` supports three diet measures: MEPA, DASH, and HEI-2015.
Each describes diet quality in a different way. The package first calculates
or accepts a diet score, then applies the LE8 scoring rules.

This article explains where the measures came from, how they become LE8
points, and which inputs to use. Examples apply to adults aged 20 or older.

## Where the diet measures came from

### MEPA: a short dietary screener

The Mediterranean Eating Pattern for Americans (MEPA) tool asks about foods
associated with a Mediterranean-style eating pattern. It was evaluated by
[Cerwinske and colleagues in 2017](https://doi.org/10.1111/jhn.12451).
The AHA adapted it for rapid individual assessment in its
[2022 LE8 advisory](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10503546/).

`essential8` implements the advisory's modified 16-item version. Each item
earns zero or one point, giving a total from 0 to 16. Fixed bands convert
that total to LE8 points. No population comparison is needed. The
[Get Started vignette](essential8-get-started.html) covers the MEPA inputs.

### DASH: an eating pattern and a research score

DASH stands for Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension. The eating pattern
was tested in an [NHLBI-supported feeding trial](https://biolincc.nhlbi.nih.gov/studies/dash/)
to study its effects on blood pressure. It emphasizes fruits, vegetables,
and low-fat dairy, with less saturated and total fat.

Researchers later developed scores to measure how closely a person's diet
follows that pattern. `essential8` uses an adaptation of the eight-component
score described by [Fung and colleagues in 2008](https://doi.org/10.1001/archinte.168.7.713).
Its total ranges from 8 to 40. Other DASH scores exist, so the name "DASH"
alone does not establish that two scores use the same definition.

### HEI-2015: alignment with dietary guidelines

The Healthy Eating Index (HEI) measures how closely a diet follows the
Dietary Guidelines for Americans. USDA released the first HEI in 1995;
later versions were developed with the National Cancer Institute (NCI).
HEI-2015 reflects the 2015-2020 guidelines and has 13 components that sum
to a score from 0 to 100. See the [NCI history and standards](https://epi.grants.cancer.gov/hei/developing.html).

HEI-2015 rewards foods and nutrients to include, such as whole grains and
vegetables, and limits others, such as sodium and added sugars. Most
components use intake per 1,000 kcal, so eating more food does not by itself
produce a higher score. The package uses HEI-2015 because that is the version
specified in the 2022 LE8 definition.

## How diet scores become LE8 points

The AHA advisory uses modified MEPA for individual assessment and DASH or
HEI-2015 for population assessment. These are alternative ways to score the
**same LE8 diet component**. They do not add extra components to LE8.

| Diet measure | Original score | How it becomes an LE8 diet score |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Modified MEPA | 0-16 | Apply fixed MEPA bands |
| Fung-style DASH | 8-40 | Compare the total with a reference population |
| HEI-2015 | 0-100 | Compare the total with a reference population |

A raw diet score, also called an index, is the total before conversion to
LE8 points.

For DASH and HEI-2015, a percentile describes a score's position in the
reference population. For example, the 75th percentile marks the upper
quarter of that distribution. The advisory assigns LE8 points as follows:

| MEPA total | DASH or HEI-2015 percentile | LE8 diet points |
|:--|:--|--:|
| 0-3 | Below 25 | 0 |
| 4-7 | 25 to below 50 | 25 |
| 8-11 | 50 to below 75 | 50 |
| 12-14 | 75 to below 95 | 80 |
| 15-16 | 95 or higher | 100 |

These bands come from the [AHA LE8 advisory, Table 1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10503546/).
A raw HEI-2015 score of 70 is therefore different from the 70th percentile
or an LE8 diet score of 70. The reference determines which LE8 band contains
that raw score.

The resulting `le8_diet_score` contributes to the LE8 composite in the same
way as the other seven components. `score_le8()` averages available component
scores when at least `min_components` are present; the default is seven.

## What the packaged reference represents

The advisory initially recommends NHANES 2015-2018 as the reference for
population diet scoring. NHANES is the National Health and Nutrition
Examination Survey. `essential8` includes references derived from those
survey years and the matching USDA Food Patterns Equivalents Database
(FPED), which converts foods into common food-group units.

The package references describe 8,241 adults aged 20 or older, excluding
known pregnancy, with two reliable dietary recalls and complete required
inputs. The builder averages the same two days' foods, nutrients, and energy
before scoring. It uses the combined dietary weight (`WTDR2D / 2`), survey
strata, and sampling units to calculate weighted cutpoints: the score values
that mark the percentile boundaries.

These are estimates calculated for this package, rather than cutpoint tables
published by the AHA. They describe scores based on two recalls, rather than
each person's long-term usual intake. Scoring uses the stored cutpoints;
it does not download data or rank the people in your input against each other.

The DASH reference uses the package's specific FPED adaptation,
`essential8_fung_fped_v1`. It uses pooled intake quintiles across sexes and
the food definitions listed below. An existing DASH score must match these
definitions to use this reference. HEI-2015 inputs should also match the
reference's method of combining recalls.

## Choose the inputs you have

Use one diet method and one type of diet input per call:

| Available data | What to supply |
|:--|:--|
| MEPA responses | The 16 screener items with `diet_method = "mepa"` |
| DASH or HEI-2015 food and nutrient summaries | The raw input columns described below |
| An existing DASH or HEI-2015 score | A column named `dash` or `hei2015` |
| An existing percentile | A column named `diet_value`, using 0-100 percentile points |

The examples use `dplyr` and the native pipe (`|>`, available in R 4.1+).
We start with two packaged example adults so the other LE8 components are
available. All records and added diet values are illustrative. The selected
method ignores the unused MEPA columns in these records.

```{r example-data}
library(essential8)
library(dplyr)

example_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "le8-adult-example.csv", package = "essential8"
)

adults <- read.csv(example_file) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  slice_head(n = 2) |>
  select(-starts_with("expected_")) |>
  mutate(id = c("adult_1", "adult_2"))
```

### An existing diet score

Add an HEI-2015 score and name the reference explicitly:

```{r existing-score}
adults |>
  mutate(hei2015 = c(45, 70)) |>
  score_le8(diet_method = "hei2015", reference = "nhanes_2015_2018") |>
  select(id, hei2015, le8_diet_score)
```

The raw scores of 45 and 70 receive 25 and 80 LE8 points with this reference.
For an existing DASH score, use a `dash` column and `diet_method = "dash"`.
The original score stays in its input column; `dash_total` and
`hei2015_total` are filled only when calculated from raw inputs.

### An existing percentile

A percentile already contains the population comparison, so no reference
lookup is needed:

```{r existing-percentile}
adults |>
  mutate(diet_value = c(35, 98)) |>
  score_le8(diet_method = "dash") |>
  select(id, diet_value, le8_diet_score)
```

These percentiles receive 25 and 100 LE8 points. Supply `95` for the 95th
percentile, rather than `0.95`. The package rejects a batch that looks like
fractional proportions and does not rescale it. This check can also reject
genuine fractional percentiles below 1 when they make up the whole batch.
The generic `diet_method = "percentile"` option uses the same LE8 bands.

## Calculate DASH from raw inputs

The Fung-style score compares each of eight intakes with reference
quintiles: five intake groups, each containing about one fifth of the
reference population. Fruit, vegetables, nuts and legumes, whole grains,
and low-fat dairy earn 1-5 points as intake increases. Sodium, red and
processed meat, and sweetened beverages earn 5-1 points. The eight scores
sum to `dash_total`.

There are two population comparisons here: intake quintiles create the
DASH total, then total-score cutpoints assign the LE8 band. Both come from
the packaged reference by default.

### Prepare the daily inputs

For the packaged reference, use these FPED-based definitions. Cup and ounce
equivalents are standardized food-group amounts, not necessarily the volume
or weight of the food as eaten.

| Column | Daily input |
|:--|:--|
| `dash_fruits` | Total fruit cup equivalents, including juice |
| `dash_vegetables` | Dark-green cup equivalents plus twice the sum of red/orange, other, and other-starchy vegetable cup equivalents; exclude white potatoes and legumes |
| `dash_nuts_and_legumes` | Protein ounce equivalents from legumes, nuts/seeds, and soy |
| `dash_whole_grains` | Whole-grain ounce equivalents |
| `dash_low_fat_dairy` | Skim-milk cup equivalents plus four times low-fat cheese cup equivalents, plus yogurt cup equivalents, using the reference's food-code lists |
| `dash_sodium` | Sodium in mg/day |
| `dash_red_and_processed_meat` | Cured-meat ounce equivalents divided by 1.5 plus meat/organ ounce equivalents divided by 4 |
| `dash_sweetened_beverages` | Added-sugar teaspoon equivalents from the reference's beverage codes, multiplied by 4/26 |
| `dash_energy_kcal` | Positive kcal/day, including alcohol |

The package standardizes sodium to 2,000 kcal using
`sodium / energy_kcal * 2000`. Supply unadjusted mg/day; do not apply this
adjustment twice. Average the same recalls' daily inputs before scoring.

### Score the inputs

```{r raw-dash}
dash_inputs <- tibble(
  dash_fruits = c(1, 2),
  dash_vegetables = c(2, 3),
  dash_nuts_and_legumes = c(0.5, 1),
  dash_whole_grains = c(1, 2),
  dash_low_fat_dairy = c(1, 2),
  dash_sodium = c(3000, 2000),
  dash_red_and_processed_meat = c(1, 0.5),
  dash_sweetened_beverages = c(1, 0),
  dash_energy_kcal = c(2000, 2000)
)

adults |>
  bind_cols(dash_inputs) |>
  score_le8(diet_method = "dash", reference = "nhanes_2015_2018") |>
  select(id, dash_total, le8_diet_score)
```

## Calculate HEI-2015 from raw inputs

HEI-2015 uses fixed nutrition standards to calculate its raw score. Its
nine adequacy components cover fruit, vegetables, whole grains, dairy,
protein foods, and the balance of unsaturated to saturated fats. Its four
moderation components cover refined grains, sodium, added sugars, and
saturated fats. Each component contributes up to 5 or 10 points, for a
maximum total of 100. See the [NCI scoring standards](https://epi.grants.cancer.gov/hei/developing.html).

Scores between the minimum and maximum standards are proportional. For
example, 0.8 cup equivalents of total fruit per 1,000 kcal earns all 5
fruit points; 0.4 earns 2.5. Higher intake beyond a component's maximum
standard does not add points. After summing the 13 components, the package
compares the total with the reference to assign LE8 points.

### Prepare the daily inputs

| Columns, all prefixed with `hei2015_` | Units |
|:--|:--|
| `energy_kcal` | Positive kcal/day, including alcohol |
| `total_fruits`, `whole_fruits`, `total_vegetables`, `greens_and_beans`, `dairy` | Cup equivalents/day |
| `whole_grains`, `total_protein_foods`, `seafood_and_plant_proteins`, `refined_grains` | Ounce equivalents/day |
| `polyunsaturated_fat`, `monounsaturated_fat`, `saturated_fat` | Grams/day |
| `sodium` | mg/day |
| `added_sugars` | Teaspoon equivalents/day |

Include juice in total fruit but exclude it from whole fruit. Count legumes
in both vegetable and protein groups, using the appropriate equivalents.
Average the same recalls' inputs before scoring. The package calculates the
densities, fat ratio, and energy percentages from these amounts, following
the [NCI algorithm](https://epi.grants.cancer.gov/hei/hei-scoring-method.html).

### Score the inputs

```{r raw-hei}
hei_inputs <- tibble(
  hei2015_energy_kcal = c(2000, 2000),
  hei2015_total_fruits = c(1, 2),
  hei2015_whole_fruits = c(0.5, 1),
  hei2015_total_vegetables = c(2, 3),
  hei2015_greens_and_beans = c(0.2, 0.5),
  hei2015_whole_grains = c(1, 3),
  hei2015_dairy = c(2, 3),
  hei2015_total_protein_foods = c(5, 5),
  hei2015_seafood_and_plant_proteins = c(1, 2),
  hei2015_polyunsaturated_fat = c(15, 20),
  hei2015_monounsaturated_fat = c(20, 25),
  hei2015_saturated_fat = c(25, 15),
  hei2015_refined_grains = c(5, 3),
  hei2015_sodium = c(3000, 2000),
  hei2015_added_sugars = c(12, 8)
)

adults |>
  bind_cols(hei_inputs) |>
  score_le8(diet_method = "hei2015", reference = "nhanes_2015_2018") |>
  select(id, hei2015_total, le8_diet_score)
```

Raw HEI-2015 scoring also returns all 13 component scores, such as
`hei2015_total_fruits_score` and `hei2015_sodium_score`.

## Use a different reference when needed

For existing scores or raw HEI-2015 inputs, `diet_reference()` defines
total-score cutpoints at the 25th, 50th, 75th, and 95th percentiles:

```{r custom-reference}
# Teaching values only; derive real cutpoints from a suitable population.
custom <- diet_reference(
  p25 = 40, p50 = 55, p75 = 65, p95 = 80,
  method = "hei2015", label = "Example reference"
)

adults |>
  mutate(hei2015 = c(45, 70)) |>
  score_le8(diet_method = "hei2015", reference = custom) |>
  select(id, hei2015, le8_diet_score)
```

A reference must match the diet method, score definition, and population.
For raw DASH with a different definition, supply `dash_cutpoints`: a list
with four intake-quintile cutpoints for each of the eight fields and four
total-score cutpoints in `total`. A reference containing only total-score
cutpoints cannot define the intake quintiles.

Explicit `dash_cutpoints` or `hei2015_cutpoints` bypass `reference`. With
explicit DASH cutpoints, input units must match those used to derive the
cutpoints. Energy is not required and sodium is not standardized. For raw
HEI-2015, `hei2015_cutpoints` is a vector of four total-score cutpoints.

Tied cutpoints are allowed. Equality with an intake-quintile cutpoint stays
in the lower quintile; equality with a total-score cutpoint enters the
higher LE8 band. The four total cutpoints identify bands, not an exact
percentile for every possible score.

## Practical details

- Choose one method per call. Do not combine raw inputs with an existing
  index or observed percentile. An entirely missing `diet_value` column is
  ignored.
- For custom column names, use mappings such as
  `dash_columns = c(fruits = "fruit_intake", energy_kcal = "calories")`.
  `hei2015_columns` works the same way. Names are matched without regard
  to case.
- Missing inputs stay missing. A raw total requires all its components;
  `min_components` controls the LE8 composite, not a partial diet total.
  Available HEI component scores are still returned.

See `?score_le8` for the full input rules. The repository's
[reference documentation](https://github.com/thatoneguy006/essential8/blob/HEAD/data-raw/README.md)
records the FPED conversions, food-code lists, sample selection, and survey
methods. Its build script and source manifest record how the packaged
references were produced.
